chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But [He granted authority] over those who take him as their guardian and disobey His command.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُمْ: Those who take him as guardian/ally

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Satan having authority over believers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) clarification that Satan’s *sultan* (authority/power) is not inherent but contingent upon human free will, distinguishing between those who voluntarily submit to his whispers and those who remain steadfast in faith. This hadith underscores the Shia theological principle that *wilayah* and conscious obedience serve as a shield against satanic influence, while negligence opens the door to his dominion. It reinforces the concept of *taklif* (accountability) by showing that spiritual status is dynamic, dependent on the believer's active choice to resist or yield.
